How to Calculate Your Break-Even Selling Price

Find the price where revenue approximately equals all selling costs.

A break-even price is the sale price at which estimated profit reaches zero. When fees are a percentage of the selling price, you cannot simply add that percentage to your costs.

Break-even price = fixed costs ÷ (1 − percentage fee rate)

If fixed costs total $34 and percentage fees are 15%, break-even is $34 ÷ 0.85 = $40. A fee assumption of 100% or more makes a finite break-even price impossible.

Use the break-even calculator to combine item cost, shipping, fixed fees, and other costs correctly.

What break-even does not include

Unless you enter them, the result will not include returns, income taxes, your labor, inventory storage, or general overhead. Treat it as a planning estimate and verify the fee rules that apply to your transaction.

Keep the estimate honest.

Fee structures and actual costs can change. Verify the rules that apply to your sale and treat every result as planning information.
